frequency_question: How often do major, highly contested executive fee-structure regulations successfully reach final publication in the Federal Register within 272 days of proposal under similar political conditions?
membership_rule: Includes major rules published by DHS, DOL, or USCIS that alter fee structures by orders of magnitude; excludes routine annual inflation adjustments and sub-regulatory guidance.

cases.name: DOL H-1B Wage Level Rule (Interim Final)

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 3 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 3 named; represents the complete set of comparable high-magnitude first-term immigration rulemakings executed via expedited or aggressive notice-and-comment.
known_gaps: Does not capture extreme financial magnitude ($103k fee is unprecedentedly high compared to previous fee adjustments which were under 100% increases).
skeleton: Three distinct aggressive immigration-related regulatory pushes during the first Trump administration that bypassed conventional gradualism, each taking roughly 6 to 9 months from conceptual rollout to Federal Register publication.
multiplier: 3 hits out of 3 comparable aggressive regulatory pushes equals 1.00 base rate for agency output, tempered by judicial friction.
validity_reason: Base rate tied directly to executive agency operational speed and administrative procedures act constraints under a specific presidential administration style.
